items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And I had him, I got him his first job with the tuxedo.

ctx.x: I'll find different spokes when I was writing. I'll find the snare drums sound more like Kittle drums. Long time ago they used to sound like a bunch of shots. Yeah. A kid.

That's what Dixon was on. Yeah, that's a short sound job. And I'll tell you, I'm going to tell you the reason that, Manuel, and you know it. Our drummers would play it in our jazz band, in our rag-tonged band those days. They tuned, they know how to tune those snares. See, you got to tune those snares. The snares got to be gauged, just like the strings on a violin, on a bass violin. They got to be tuned, and you got a row of snares on them things, and the snares all got to be correct, not too loose, they all got…

items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...And Pop Foster says the same thing.

ctx.x: Yes that's when he sang that 'Black and Blue' and all that stuff.

But personally there was a little jealousy in those days with Louis. And that's what Barney (Bonnie?) says all the time, Louis was jealous you know. And Pop Foster says the same thing. And EARVELL SHAW says the same thing you know and all. But the show girls, the dancing girls, the acts the hits, they loved Zuddy so, you know. They wanted, they hadn't had anybody they said to play like that for them. And I think that made Louis feel like Zuddy was ...........
Oh, you mean he was very popular with the people in the show?
